content:
amanda: spotting a small but urgent issue in today's usage billing run — ~320 customers billed for extra 'high-throughput' units they didn't use. totals ~ $7.4k.

rishi: that's bad. any hypothesis?

lydia: correlated with the pricing-experiment that toggled the new meter-label logic yesterday morning. product said it's backwards-compatible.

amanda: sample customer invoice shows line: 
```
Product: Redwood Inference - HighThroughput Units x 50 @ $0.20 = $10.00
```
But usage dashboard shows 0 high-throughput usage for that org.

qa-bot: automated check: experiment flag 'meter_label_v2' enabled at 2026-06-05T06:15Z for 40% of traffic. Billing job uses meter_key -> plan mapping from the mapping table.

rishi: do we have a mapping drift? maybe the new label collided with existing meter_key for a different unit.

amanda: looking at the usage ingestion logs:
```
2026-06-05T06:17:03Z usage_ingest: record id=u_9abc; meter_label='high_throughput_v2'; resolved_key='high_throughput' -> plan_id=P-HT-STD
2026-06-05T06:17:03Z usage_ingest: record id=u_9abd; meter_label='high_throughput_v2'; resolved_key='ht_backup' -> plan_id=P-HT-BACKUP
```
Seems resolution service returned different resolved_key for different shards.

tom: would that cause Stripe to create usage records under two different pricing items? yes. If NetSuite reconciler expects one canonical plan mapping, duplicates or mismatches happen.

lydia: product: the experiment added a fallback resolution that prefers an internal alias if canonical not found. that alias collided with an older plan key used by a past migration.

amanda: consequences: Stripe usage records were created for plan-item P-HT-BACKUP for some customers; our NetSuite ingestion pipeline couldn't map that plan-id to subscription lines (we only map P-HT-STD), so invoices got generated with an unrecognized line which later our billing-worker attempted to migrate as ADJ leading to extra charges.

rishi: can you paste the ingestion trace for a single affected customer?

amanda: sure:
```
cust=org_3421
2026-06-05T06:18:11Z -> usage_ingest created usage_record id=u_9c33 plan_item=P-HT-BACKUP quantity=50
2026-06-05T06:18:15Z -> stripe.usage_record.create succeeded: id=ur_5xyz
2026-06-05T07:05:03Z -> netsuite_ingest: failed to associate plan_item=P-HT-BACKUP -> created AR line as 'Unmapped usage' (INV-20988)
2026-06-05T07:06:30Z -> billing-worker attempted auto-map -> applied price fallback -> double-counted in reconciliation
```

qa-bot: bulk scan: 320 invoices with 'Unmapped usage' line, 310 resolved by auto-mapping heuristics later but 10 remained open and led to customer disputes.

lydia: immediate mitigation: disable experiment flag for meter_label_v2 (turn off at rollout control). Also pause the nightly billing job to prevent another run.

ops-bot: billing job paused at 2026-06-05T08:40Z by ops.

amanda: next steps I propose: 
- flip experiment off immediately (assign product / lydia)
- run a mapping backfill that maps P-HT-BACKUP -> P-HT-STD for affected customer subscriptions and void the unmapped AR lines (assign rishi)
- create a safety check in the ingestion pipeline to error if resolved_key is not in approved canonical set (assign tom)
- add a daily monitor for 'Unmapped usage' count > 0.2% to alert finance (assign amanda)

rishi: agree. also add a reconciliation step that verifies Stripe usage item id -> netsuite plan lookup before creating invoice lines; if mismatch, flag for manual review rather than auto-apply.

lydia: product will disable flag now and roll a patch to remove alias fallback. will post when done.

(lydia toggles experiment control)
lydia: turned off meter_label_v2 at 2026-06-05T08:55Z.

amanda: performing a dry-run backfill to map affected invoices now. dry-run output sample:
```
would-map: INV-20988 line 3 -> map P-HT-BACKUP to P-HT-STD; would-void: CreditMemo candidate CM-5012
would-skip: INV-21012 line 2 -> manual review required (amount=$1,350)
```

rishi: finance policy: auto-fix only if line_amount < $1,000. anything above manual approval.

amanda: backfill run scheduled in 90 minutes during low-traffic window. attaching CSV to FIN ticket FIN-2026-PRC-07.

tom: I'll add an ingestion unit test to assert resolved_key ∈ canonical_keys and fail fast on unknown keys. will also add telemetry to surface new keys.

billing-bot: Scan summary: 320 affected invoices, estimated revenue impact $7,400, 10 disputes opened by customers, incident FIN-2026-PRICING-03 created.

qa-bot: recommend a postmortem that captures: test coverage gap, experiment rollout checklist updates (routing for billing), and a rollback guard to stop experiments that affect meter keys.

amanda: thanks everyone. please comment on the FIN ticket with any blockers. I'll reconvene after backfill results.

lydia: postmortem and runbook PR incoming. closing thread for now.
